name: Bothriochloa

project_scope.selection_mode: B027 strict review + B146 source-concept reconciliation
project_scope.note: Texas project source usage of plain Bothriochloa laguroides is treated as legacy/broad silver-bluestem usage and represented by canonical B. torreyana. Current B. laguroides sensu stricto is a separate Mexico–South America concept and is not a fourth Texas learner species.

recognition.where_to_look_first: First compare terminal head architecture (KR LONG fingers / CANE fanlike branches / SILVER narrow cottony MANY SHORT rames). Then find true stem nodes: CANE has a dramatic beard; SILVER usually pale smooth; KR's short nodal hair descriptions vary. Finish at the leaf collar and attached spikelets.
priority: terminal 3–8 long KR flowering racemes versus many short native rames
conspicuous heavy nodal beard of native cane bluestem
densely silvery cottony head of native silver bluestem
papilla-based blade hairs just above KR collar
many short rames versus a few long fingerlike branches
contracted cottony head versus broad fanlike head
awn and spikelet detail for confirmation

quick_split: CANE / B. barbinodis — a HEAVY LONG WHITE HAIR BEARD at real culm nodes + BROAD silvery FAN of many primary branches. Main native look-alike of KR; photograph the node.
SILVER / B. torreyana — PALE typically SMOOTH nodes + NARROW cottony plume of >10 SHORT hairy rames. Canonical native-range label is UNRESOLVED, not project PASS.
KR / B. ischaemum — INTRODUCED/INVASIVE project comparison; multiple LONG slender terminal fingers and papilla-based blade hairs near collar. Do NOT require hairless nodes.
LITTLE / Schizachyrium scoparium — many separate SHORT hairy racemes arising from different upper leafy branches, usually a tight bunch.
BIG / Andropogon gerardi — relatively stout exposed fingers usually 2–6, commonly turkey-foot.
BUSHY / Anatherum glomeratum — broad, dense brushy crown of short paired silky racemes partly associated with spathes.
INDIANGRASS / Sorghastrum nutans — ONE branched panicle with pointed membranous 'rifle sight' ligule rather than grouped racemes.
comparison_lesson.close_family_tie: Schizachyrium scoparium branches its upper culm into many short terminal fuzzy racemes rather than concentrating the seedhead into the Bothriochloa patterns above.

look_here_first: CANE: thick nodal HAIR BEARD + FAN head. SILVER: smooth pale node + NARROW silver cotton head (>10 short rames). KR: several LONG terminal fingers, stiff papilla-based blade hairs. Fuzzy head alone never proves a species.

cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.title: KR BLUESTEM vs LITTLE BLUESTEM — our Central Texas native/invasive decision
cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.memory_rule: A FEW LONG fingers together (KR) versus MANY SHORT fuzzy racemes on SEPARATE upper branches (little bluestem).
quick_split: KR / Bothriochloa ischaemum — introduced Old World bluestem; terminal panicle typically 3–8 or more elongated fingerlike spikelet-bearing branches. Leaf UPPER surface just above collar may have stiff papilla-based hairs. Node hair sources conflict; not a single-character proof.

Little bluestem / Schizachyrium scoparium — Hays native, generally dense persistent bunch; many short racemes arise from different branches in the upper plant and become silvery/fluffy in fruit. Roots/leaf collar and actual spikelet pairs strengthen ID.
field_crew_sequence: Photograph rooted whole clump and top-to-bottom reproductive architecture.
Trace WHERE each raceme originates: all near one terminal center = KR candidate; dispersed short units on many upper culm branches = little bluestem candidate.
At 10×, inspect KR upper leaf surface right above collar for papilla-based hairs; check true ligule on same culm.
Check paired sessile fertile/pedicelled companion spikelet details with 1-mm scale; where unresolved label bluestem sp.
Before removal or seed collection, rule out native cane bluestem and silver bluestem plus introduced Kleberg bluestem.
cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.node_hair_caution: Do not enforce smooth KR nodes: Texas A&M calls songarica nodes hairless; local UT Austin morphological work reports short or appressed hairs. Use combined characters. Cane bluestem tends to bear a pronounced BEARD at nodes.

cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.first_clue: KR bluestem (introduced): look for several long, slender fingerlike flowering branches clustered together at the tip of a stem. Native little bluestem has shorter fuzzy flowering branches along separate upper stems.

expert_collar_and_node_notes.Leaf collar: On a confirmed same-plant specimen, inspect stiff papilla-based hairs on the upper leaf blade near the collar; photograph the true ligule with a ruler.
expert_collar_and_node_notes.Spikelet pairs: At 10–20× magnification, separate an attached sessile fertile spikelet from its pedicelled companion and check the awn; the current photos do not resolve this.
expert_collar_and_node_notes.Node-hair caution: Do NOT use hairless stem nodes as a required test. Texas A&M describes glabrous KR nodes, while local UT Austin treatments have noted short hairs. A heavy beard is useful when considering native cane bluestem.
expert_collar_and_node_notes.Native versus invasive decision: Use multiple characters and preserve the project's nonnative invasive-comparison status; never remove native bluestem on a seedhead silhouette alone.

multi_species_field_atlas.title: Central Texas bluestem and Indiangrass — 8 encountered species
multi_species_field_atlas.first_decision: Does the upper head form long terminal fingers, separate short silky racemes, a broad brush/fan, or one panicle? Photograph head origin and true nodes.

species.first_look: Several LONG thin fingerlike racemes in a terminal cluster; stiff papilla-based hairs on upper leaf blade near collar support ID
species.caution: Introductory invasive/introduced comparison. Node hairs variable; do NOT use hairless nodes as decisive.

species.first_look: MANY SHORT silky racemes occur separately on branching upper leafy stems; often a tight clump
species.caution: Do not ID from autumn red color alone.

species.first_look: Usually 2–6 relatively STOUT exposed racemes near one terminal point, often turkey-foot
species.caution: KR can also have multiple terminal fingers; compare stoutness, branching and leaf collar.

species.first_look: Dense broad BRUSH of crowded short silky paired racemes, subtended by spathe-like leafy sheaths
species.caution: Can resemble broomsedge or silver bluestem before flowering is fully developed.

species.first_look: Dense long soft hair BEARD at stem nodes plus broad FAN of many silvery branches
species.caution: Node must be from the same flowering plant; a fuzzy head alone is insufficient.

species.first_look: Narrow contracted COTTONY SILVER head of >10 short rames; pale usually smooth nodes
species.caution: This project currently has native-range UNRESOLVED, not target-zone certified PASS.

species.first_look: Single narrow-to-open golden BRANCHED PANICLE and conspicuous pointed membranous 'rifle-sight' ligule
species.caution: Examine attached fertile spikelet and sterile pedicel; panicle color alone not enough.

species.first_look: Relatively narrow silky inflorescence of paired rames partly held in long flattened spathe-like sheaths
species.caution: Existing species is canonical; compare directly against bushy bluestem.

decision_flow.question: One golden elongated BRANCHED panicle and tall rifle-sight membranous ligule?
Several exposed fingers near one terminal point?
decision_flow.yes: KR if thin/long and stiff hairs near collar; big bluestem if fewer stout turkey-foot fingers; inspect spikelets.

decision_flow.question: Short silky racemes repeated on separate upper leafy branches?
decision_flow.no: Check brushy, fanlike, or cottony head and stem nodes.

decision_flow.question: Dramatic soft white hair beard around true stem nodes?
decision_flow.yes: Bothriochloa barbinodis candidate; broad fan supports
decision_flow.no: Narrow cottony densely short-branched head suggests B. torreyana; broad compact brush with spathes suggests Anatherum glomeratum.

decision_flow.question: Narrow individually spathe-held hairy units rather than broad bushy crown?
decision_flow.no: Unresolved: sample attached fertile spikelets, collar and node; label bluestem sp.

multi_species_field_atlas.management_caution: Never make KR removal decisions from head fluff or fall color alone; do a genuine head+collar+stem node exam. Avoid exposing held photos or making county native certification from provisional comparison taxa.

items.label: Silver bluestem — silvery contracted narrow head
items.image_role: 2018 New Mexico source-labelled wild type photographed as Bothriochloa laguroides subsp. torreyana
items.caption: A dense cottony, pale silvery inflorescence contains many short branches along a central flowering axis. The original photo lacks a visible true stem node or measured spikelet pair.
items.why_it_matters: Separates its narrow cottony cluster from cane's many-branched broad fan and KR's long fingerlike racemes.

items.label: KR bluestem — 3 radiating long racemes
items.image_role: Actual archived source-labelled photo, several long flowering branches spreading from clustered lower portion
items.caption: Three distinct long, narrow flowering racemes and their approximate convergence are visible against the hand. The vegetative stem node, ligule, papilla-based blade hairs and microscopic spikelets are off-camera.
items.why_it_matters: Shows how separate long racemes converge toward one clustered reproductive head, unlike scattered short axillary racemes of little bluestem.
items.creator: Sam Kieschnick
items.photo_status: Existing local JPEG physically inspected and only gross head architecture annotated; exact CC BY version unresolved.

items.label: Little bluestem — separate short silky racemes on upper flowering shoots
items.image_role: Source-labelled Montana wild-type little bluestem, close-up of flowering branches bearing distinct short silky racemes and subtending sheaths
items.caption: At the branch tips, each narrow pale hairy raceme emerges from a reddish leaf-sheath/spathe area. The feathery hairs along the short spikelet-bearing axes are visible, but individual sessile versus reduced pedicelled spikelets, the real basal ligule, and precise awn lengths cannot be confirmed from this photograph.
items.why_it_matters: Shows the SHORT flowering units along DIFFERENT upper branches, instead of KR bluestem's several LONG fingerlike racemes collected in one terminal cluster.
items.creator: Matt Lavin
items.photo_status: Exact 960×1280 Wikimedia thumbnail viewed and licensed source file checked 2026-10-21; photo from Montana; original label Andropogon scoparius is accepted synonym of Schizachyrium scoparium; visible gross arrows only, not microscopy.
